chunks: From him, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from his grandfather Muawiya ibn Wahb, or someone else, from Razin, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Muslims, when they went on military expedition with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and passed by a place with many trees, then went out to the open space, some of them would look at each other and shake hands.
ai.seo_question: What was the customary greeting among Muslims after returning from military expeditions in the time of the Prophet?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s era custom of shaking hands upon returning from battle, symbolizing relief and renewed brotherhood after the trials of war. In Shia scholarship, this act is often cited as evidence for the permissibility and virtue of handshaking (muṣāfaha) as a means of fostering social cohesion and expressing mutual respect among believers. The gesture underscores the importance of maintaining communal bonds and spiritual connection even in the aftermath of physical exertion and conflict.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from his grandfather Muawiya Bin Wahab, or someone else, from Razyn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was so that whenever the Muslims used to go on a military expedition with Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and pass by a place with a lot of trees, then go out to the open sky, some of them used to look at the others and shake their hands’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Musa ibn al-Qasim from his grandfather, Mu’awiyah ibn Wahab or from others from Razin from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“During an armed expedition the Muslims, along with the Messenger of Allah, each time after passing through a wooded area on reaching the open would look at each other and shake hands.”
